questions.explanation: (1) Electrolytes conduct electricity due to the movement of ions in a solution. When an electrolyte dissolves in water, it dissociates into positive and negative ions, which move toward the respective electrodes under the influence of an electric field. This ionic movement allows the current to pass through the solution. Electrons flow in metallic conductors (like wires), not in electrolytic solutions. Hence, the correct mechanism in electrolytes is ionic conduction.
